usage: Statement ids, payload bytes, pin digests and authority roots are deterministic and MUST reproduce exactly. Signatures are verification only (§18.3.2; see ed25519-strict-v2.json): check that each verifies over its payload; never sign and compare bytes. For every case, resolve the listed statements in any order, and in every order, and reproduce expected.status, inForce, live, keptBy (the bucket that keeps each in-force statement: its own, or its rescuer's), roles and root. A case with testQuota or testDelegateQuota uses that value in place of AUTHORITY_QUOTA or AUTHORITY_DELEGATE_QUOTA. lifecycle is informative: what each subject may advance a CMB to outside every scope, and inside each scope it holds.
warning: all private seeds are fixed conformance fixtures; never use them as identities

cases.label: a delegation tree is in force
a grantor above revokes: the admin removes a participant two hops below it
the anchor removes the admin: everything the admin authorised is dead
the anchor endorses the admin's validator and its revoke: both survive, the admin does not
an admin beside the removed one cannot endorse its subtree
an admin removes its validator and keeps one of the validator's grants, in its own bucket
an endorse is never rescued, so an endorse that names an endorse keeps nothing
a fresh grant does not revive the old grant's dependents
a revoke from off the chain removes nothing
invalid statements are inert
authorisedBy must name a grant: one naming a revoke is pending while the revoke is not held, invalid once it is
a statement whose chain is not held is pending and changes nothing
the chain arrives and the pending statement is in force
a hosted world four hops below the anchor, scoped to one world; scopes only narrow; an issuer grants seats only; a fifth hop is too deep
issuers are delegating grants: a world admin's bucket keeps 16 of 17, by id
rescue falls through: the lower endorser's bucket is full, so the next endorser keeps the grant (test parameter quota = 3)
an issuer revokes a seat it granted
a single-key anchor is the 1-of-1 case, and its holder resolves as anchor
under a threshold of 1 every pinned member alone is the anchor
at the quota a bucket keeps removals first, then grants by ascending id (test parameter quota = 2)
an over-quota revoke removes nothing (test parameter quota = 2)
a bucket keeps at most the delegate quota of delegating grants, decided by id; the anchor's bucket is exempt (test parameter delegateQuota = 1)
copies of an anchor statement are judged one by one, never merged
one copy that meets the threshold makes the statement valid
an endorse does not override a revoke
rescue reaches past a dead grant to the revoke that cut it off
a revoke acts target by target: on its chain it removes, off it and on a revoke it does nothing
review attack r2: admins hung under over-quota grants are dead, never rescued
review attack r2 laundered: the admin revokes its own over-quota grants, and their rescue is charged to its full delegate quota
a rescue that fits: rescued delegating grants take the endorser's free delegate slots, by id
review attack r1 at test scale: depth-3 admins under over-quota grants stay dead (test parameters quota = 4, delegateQuota = 2)
review attack r1 at test scale, laundered (test parameters quota = 4, delegateQuota = 2)
the bound is reached by a full tree (test parameters quota = 2, delegateQuota = 1)
and not exceeded by extra grants, a laundering revoke and a rescue (test parameters quota = 2, delegateQuota = 1)
